scenario.title: Alstom Transport UK Ltd v London Underground Ltd
scenario.description: London Underground awarded contract to Bombardier for £112.1 million worth of AC traction motors and control equipment. Alstom challenged the award alleging a manifest error in applying a mandatory technical threshold requirement, which should have excluded Bombardier's bid. The challenge was brought during the standstill period, triggering an automatic suspension. London Underground applied to lift the suspension under the American Cyanamid framework, arguing that damages would be adequate remedy for Alstom if it succeeded at trial and that the balance of convenience favoured proceeding with the contract.

interests: Compliance & Legality: Act lawfully and within powers under the Procurement Act 2023 to avoid manifest error findings.
Protection of Public Funds: Avoid significant delay costs due to automatic suspension or re-run of procurement.
Continuity of Service / Delivery: Ensure delivery of £112,100,000 worth of AC traction motors and control equipment for London Underground's services.
Reputation & Public Accountability: Maintain public confidence in the procurement process and protect London Underground's reputation as a competent buyer.
ca_pre_negotiation.batna: Defend the decision in the TCC — costly (£50k+) and slow (6-12 months), with a real risk of automatic suspension.
ca_pre_negotiation.opening_position: We will defend our evaluation process, citing evidence and procedural fairness to support our mandatory technical threshold requirement.

interests: Commercial Loss & Recovery: £112.1 million contract value at stake
Fairness & Transparency: perceived unfair application of technical threshold requirement
Protection of Reputation: potential damage to Alstom's credibility in future bids
goals: Force a re-evaluation or partial award
bidder_pre_negotiation.batna: Pursue a damages claim in the TCC — costly (£50k-£100k in legal fees) for a business our size, slow, and the outcome is uncertain.
bidder_pre_negotiation.opening_position: Request detailed feedback on evaluation process to justify London Underground's decision
legal_basis: manifest error in applying technical threshold requirement

messages.message: I acknowledge Alstom's challenge and appreciate the opportunity to discuss this matter further. I would like to clarify whether you are alleging that the technical threshold requirement was applied incorrectly, or if there is another aspect of the evaluation process that you believe was flawed. Could you provide more context on what specific actions you believe led to the manifest error? Furthermore, I'd like to offer a voluntary extension of the standstill period by 7 days to allow for further engagement and discussion.
messages.concession_made: Voluntary extension of the standstill period

messages.message: Thank you for acknowledging our challenge and offering a voluntary extension of the standstill period by 7 days. I'd like to clarify what specific actions led to the manifest error, as stated in the American Cyanamid framework, which London Underground applied to lift the suspension. Could you provide more details on how you evaluated the technical threshold requirement and why you believe it was correctly applied? Additionally, can you explain your reasoning behind arguing that damages would be an adequate remedy for us if we succeeded at trial?

I'd like to provide more clarity on our evaluation process for the technical threshold requirement. We applied a mandatory technical threshold requirement, which was clearly stated in the tender documentation. The requirement specified that bidders must have at least 5 years of experience in delivering similar projects. Our evaluation team carefully reviewed each bidder's submission and determined that Bombardier met this requirement. I'd like to offer additional feedback on our evaluation process, including a detailed breakdown of how we applied the technical threshold requirement, which may help alleviate some of your concerns.
messages.concession_made: A voluntary extension of the standstill period by an additional 7 days

messages.message: I appreciate your offer to provide additional feedback on your evaluation process, including a detailed breakdown of how you applied the technical threshold requirement. However, I must express my concern that this may not be sufficient to address our concerns regarding the manifest error in applying the mandatory technical threshold requirement. We believe that a re-evaluation of all bids is necessary to ensure fairness and transparency in the procurement process. Furthermore, we would like to request clarification on how you determined that Bombardier met the 5-year experience requirement, as this seems inconsistent with our own assessment.

I understand your concerns regarding the manifest error in applying the mandatory technical threshold requirement and the need for a re-evaluation of all bids to ensure fairness and transparency. I'd like to offer a compromise: we can provide a detailed breakdown of our evaluation process, including the specific reasons why Bombardier met the 5-year experience requirement, as well as an explanation of how this requirement was applied consistently across all bidders. This may help alleviate some of your concerns regarding the manifest error.
messages.proposal: A partial re-evaluation of the bids to address Alstom's concerns
messages.concession_made: A voluntary extension of the standstill period by 7 days

messages.message: I appreciate your willingness to provide additional feedback on your evaluation process. However, I must reiterate that a detailed breakdown of how you applied the technical threshold requirement is not sufficient to address our concerns regarding the manifest error. We still believe that a re-evaluation of all bids is necessary to ensure fairness and transparency in the procurement process. Furthermore, we would like to request clarification on how you determined that Bombardier met the 5-year experience requirement, as this seems inconsistent with our own assessment.
messages.proposal: A re-evaluation of all bids, including a re-scoring of the technical threshold requirement

compliance_checks.reasoning: This scenario is qualitative, as it involves a technical threshold requirement and its application. I will assess the Contracting Authority's process based on rational justification for their decision. The Contracting Authority has offered to provide more context and details on how they evaluated the technical threshold requirement. However, without explicit numbers or scores provided in the scenario, I cannot perform a calculation. Therefore, I will rely on qualitative assessment. London Underground's argument that damages would be an adequate remedy if Alstom succeeded at trial is not directly related to the evaluation process, but rather to the American Cyanamid framework for lifting the standstill period.

applicable_provisions: s12 Procurement Act 2023 (value for money, public benefit, transparency, integrity)
compliance_checks.reasoning: This scenario is qualitative, as it involves a technical threshold requirement and experience of similar projects. There is no explicit formula or sub-scores mentioned. The Contracting Authority's position states that they applied the mandatory technical threshold requirement, which was clearly stated in the tender documentation. They also mention that their evaluation team carefully reviewed each bidder's submission and determined that Bombardier met this requirement. However, the Aggrieved Bidder raises concerns about the manifest error in applying the technical threshold requirement. I will assess compliance qualitatively, checking if the Contracting Authority's actions are rationally defensible and consistent with the published criteria.

applicable_provisions: s12 Procurement Act 2023 (value for money, public benefit, transparency, integrity)
compliance_checks.reasoning: This scenario is qualitative, not numeric. The parties' statements focus on the application of a mandatory technical threshold requirement and the evaluation process, rather than providing explicit scores or sub-scores. I will assess compliance qualitatively instead. However, I must note that the Contracting Authority's position this round does not address the manifest error in applying the technical threshold requirement. The Aggrieved Bidder's request for clarification on how Bombardier met the 5-year experience requirement also raises concerns about consistency and fairness in the evaluation process.

ca_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: The final outcome of a re-evaluation was more favorable than defending in TCC court, which would have cost £50k+ and taken 6-12 months.
ca_win_statement.win_statement: We successfully negotiated a compromise that provided additional transparency into our evaluation process without having to conduct a full re-evaluation of all bids.
what_was_achieved: Provided a detailed breakdown of the evaluation process, including the specific reasons why Bombardier met the 5-year experience requirement
Explained how the technical threshold requirement was applied consistently across all bidders
what_was_conceded: Agreed to provide additional feedback on our evaluation process
Did not insist on a full re-evaluation of all bids, despite Alstom's initial request

bidder_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: The outcome is slightly favourable to us compared to pursuing damages or formal TCC proceedings, which would have been costly, slow, and uncertain. While we did not achieve a full re-evaluation of all bids as we had requested, the contracting authority has agreed to provide additional feedback on their evaluation process, including a detailed breakdown of how they applied the technical threshold requirement.
bidder_win_statement.win_statement: We successfully negotiated an agreement that will allow us to receive additional information about the contracting authority's evaluation process, which may help alleviate some of our concerns regarding the manifest error in applying the mandatory technical threshold requirement.
what_was_achieved: A detailed breakdown of how the contracting authority applied the technical threshold requirement
Additional feedback on their evaluation process
what_was_conceded: No full re-evaluation of all bids was achieved, as requested by us
The contracting authority's position that damages would be an adequate remedy for us if we succeeded at trial remains unchanged

key_sticking_points: Consistency and fairness in evaluation process
summary.concessions_summary: The Contracting Authority made several concessions throughout the negotiation, including a voluntary extension of the standstill period by 7 days on three separate occasions. They also offered to provide additional feedback on their evaluation process, including a detailed breakdown of how they applied the technical threshold requirement.
summary.court_reasoning_summary: The Court assessed each round qualitatively, focusing on rational justification for the Contracting Authority's decisions and consistency with published criteria. In Round 3, the Court found that the Contracting Authority's position did not address the manifest error in applying the technical threshold requirement, leading to a recommendation of re-evaluation.
summary.likely_next_steps: The likely next step is a re-evaluation of all bids to ensure fairness and transparency in the procurement process. This may involve a new evaluation team or a revised evaluation methodology.
summary.plain_english_summary: The negotiation centered around the Contracting Authority's application of a technical threshold requirement, which Alstom Transport UK Ltd (the Aggrieved Bidder) challenged as being flawed. Despite concessions from the Contracting Authority, including extensions to the standstill period and additional feedback on their evaluation process, the Aggrieved Bidder continued to insist that a re-evaluation was necessary to ensure fairness and transparency.
